newsitem.title: USA: GM confirms magnesium deal with Solikamsk.
newsitem.headline: GM confirms magnesium deal with Solikamsk.

text.p: General Motors has signed a deal to buy magnesium from the Russian producer Solikamsk, a company spokesman said, confirming rumors in the market.
"We do have a contract with that company (Solikamsk)," General Motors spokesman, Tom Klipstine, told Reuters.
He declined to give any further details of the contract.
This is the second magnesium sourcing contract the automaker has signed with foreign companies.
GM has a long-term pricing and volume contract with Norsk Hydro, whose Hydro Magnesium operates facilities in Becancour, Canada and in Norway.
Solikamsk produces about 17,000 tonnes of magnesium a year and market sources estimated that GM will buy about 5,000 tonnes of alloy a year.
"I think it suits Solikamsk because it gives them a steady, projected cash flow which, for a Russian company, is more important than anything else," a dealer said.
Solikamsk's move represents a departure from the traditional Russian strategy of selling product through Western traders, according to U.S dealers and producers.

Diecast mangesium alloy automotive parts are the light metal's brightest growth prospects, but carmakers have expressed concern about the magnesium industry's ability to supply enough metal at the right price.
This concern was heightened last year when global magnesium stocks shrank to barely three week's supply and prices were very strong.

The U.S. is the world's biggest producer of primary magnesium, and market sources said domestic producers may have been reluctant to allocate a large portion of their primary output to one consumer for conversion into alloy magnesium.

Alloy is more expensive to make than primary magnesium but is sold at a discount because the industry has been effectively subsidizing the development of what is seen as a lucrative market over the coming years.
